script: I threatened to "female‑Me‑Up" after refusing a discount—now the truth is insane.. I run a used video game store with a couple of partners. We buy, sell, and trade like most of us do, but some people just cling to the "buy" part and forget the rest. A guy who'd been to our shop before called asking if we had any new PS4 games. I said we're always getting new stock, but I am not sure what's fresh, so I asked him what he was after. I don't even remember the exact title—he didn't have it in stock. He told me to scan our whole PS4 inventory. I told him I've got other customers, I can't do that. He started calling me a liar, saying he knows I am not busy because he's a store owner too. He claimed he'd seen our website, so apparently he's obsessive about our stock. Minutes later he called back, saying he saw Elden Ring on our site and asked if it was still $30. I checked real quick—yeah, we had it. He then wanted to sell back two games he'd bought and I had to bump the price up to $14. He kept bringing up $6. I asked why, he said he had store credit. I explained the tax would add about ten bucks, he got pissed. I mentioned we could offer a trade for $5. He kept getting louder, saying our trade‑ins were the best deal and that we should lower the price so he could get it. He kept saying we'd lowered prices for him before—maybe true, maybe not. He got more agitated, swore he wasn't trying to spend money, and after a few more attempts to cut our prices, he spotted God of War on the website. He asked if he could trade the first two games for it. I told him there was a difference in price. He thought I said he had $20, so he started talking over me. I tried to explain he'd get $14 for the first two games and $6 in store credit. While I was talking, he snapped, "You're pissing me off. I am not going to 'female' with my store anymore. I am going to come to your store and female me up." I called the non‑emergency police to report the threat. I was told an officer would call, but that never happened. The guy came in anyway. My partner talked to him, he apologized, and his mom—who's an adult—told him he was wrong for acting that way. We don't kick people out lightly; we've only ever done it twice for extreme reasons. He traded the games, got God of War, and admitted he understood the store credit. He just had a bad day. Hours later an officer showed up to ask about the situation, but nothing came of it.
